program.name: OBSERRA EXECUTIVE PROTECTION & INTELLIGENCE LLC Website and Academy Production Security Evidence
program.claimBoundary: Historical release-support ledger only; docs/compliance/CMMC-SYSTEM-EVIDENCE.json is the current objective-level authority. This ledger does not claim CMMC certification, CUI authorization, FedRAMP authorization, FDACS approval, or an assessor finding.

framework.currentCmmcLevel2Crosswalk: Supporting requirement identifiers only. The governing objective-level baseline is 32 CFR Part 170, the September 2024 CMMC Level 2 Assessment Guide version 2.13, NIST SP 800-171 Revision 2, and NIST SP 800-171A June 2018 as incorporated by reference; Revision 3 is supplemental forward engineering.

records.title: Explicit fail-closed identity activation and public availability isolation
records.implementation: Identity uses one server-side configuration authority, side-effect-free key inspection, conditional Clerk middleware, fail-closed protected routes, and explicit OBSERRA_IDENTITY_RUNTIME_ENABLED activation. Public content remains available when identity is disabled or degraded; identity-protected routes are not authorized without a functioning provider context.
records.boundary: Obserra application and Clerk external identity service
records.gap: Current production identity remains intentionally disabled/degraded. Verify the production Clerk instance and matching live protected configuration through the provider control plane before enabling identity, then retain post-deployment authentication and authorization evidence.

records.title: Canonical production domain binding
records.implementation: PR #80 removed repository-propagated aliases and merged as verified SHA d35917f417d24489ffd5877b989f36dbb3bbb613 after Florida Gates #570, Website CI #2344, and CodeQL #42 passed. Direct deployment inspection confirms the current duplicate-project deployments no longer carry the canonicals. Operator control-plane evidence shows both canonicals on intended project obserra-website-live and no production domain on either duplicate, but the old lcn2 deployment dpl_AYZXGVZurpGcKXLSzvKrudM7rt5w still retains both deployment-level aliases and serves canonical traffic. The liveness contract now reports VERCEL_PROJECT_ID, VERCEL_DEPLOYMENT_ID, and VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA and marks authority verified only for intended project prj_lxTKKDa9sbhht7FaigiaF1PONMiC.
records.boundary: Obserra application and Vercel edge/runtime control plane
records.gap: Deploy the routing-evidence release from the intended project, verify the live health contract reports intended project prj_lxTKKDa9sbhht7FaigiaF1PONMiC and the exact accepted deployment/commit, verify the old lcn2 deployment no longer owns either canonical alias, and retain the result before closing GitHub issue #76.

records.title: Exact-SHA production release and runtime verification
records.implementation: PR #80 exact-head validation passed Florida Class D LMS Gates #570, Website CI #2344, and CodeQL Advanced #42 before GitHub merged verified SHA d35917f417d24489ffd5877b989f36dbb3bbb613. Intended deployment dpl_DxojVNKBd9hJtcjXth3QptKei4Lw is READY and production-targeted for that exact SHA; its build compiled, type-checked, generated 159 pages, deployed output, and uploaded cache without a build error. Vercel nevertheless reports its postdeployment checks failed while lcn2 is successful, and the canonical request still reports older lcn2 deployment dpl_AYZXGVZurpGcKXLSzvKrudM7rt5w. The next release adds direct runtime project/deployment/commit evidence and requires the intended project before routing acceptance.
records.gap: Close GitHub issue #76 only after canonical traffic is exclusively bound to an accepted READY deployment in intended project prj_lxTKKDa9sbhht7FaigiaF1PONMiC and the intended Vercel postdeployment check is identified and passes. Provider-wide availability, recovery, and formal continuous-monitoring evidence remain separate requirements.

records.title: Stripe payment authorization and signed fulfillment
records.implementation: Academy Checkout Session creation is POST-only and same-origin, GET returns 405, purchase authorization and durable fulfillment health are rechecked before payment, fulfillment requires a signed Stripe webhook plus paid status, the Stripe event ID is the durable idempotency authority, and deferred redemption revalidates payment plus verified Clerk email ownership. The new contract is live, but production commerce health returns HTTP 503 with payment provider, webhook, identity, durable Academy storage, and purchaser identity hashing unavailable. Checkout and fulfillment therefore remain fail closed.
records.boundary: Obserra application and Stripe external commerce service
records.gap: Restore and verify the protected Stripe production secret and webhook secret through the provider/runtime control planes, redeploy, and retain healthy commerce and webhook evidence before production checkout is accepted.

records.title: Academy database least privilege and fail-closed publication
records.implementation: Academy service-only data paths use forced RLS and no client grants. The live main project includes four empty Academy learner-commerce tables, nine service-only functions with controlled search paths, and append-only learner and assessment audit triggers. Public catalog access is GET-only and field-limited, missing control data fails closed, and the reviewed production baseline contains 60 public/purchasable nonregulated courses with zero Class D-like controls.
records.gap: Authoritative backup, restore, retention, RPO, RTO, and provider assurance evidence remain external.

records.title: CMMC Level 2 Rev. 3 no-drift traceability
records.implementation: The authoritative control registers and production evidence are machine-readable JSON. Gate 35 separately enumerates all 110 Rev. 2 requirements, 97 active Rev. 3 requirements, and 33 withdrawn Rev. 3 identifiers. Human audit views and SHA-256 digests are generated deterministically, and CI fails on malformed mappings, missing evidence references, generated-document drift, or digest drift.
records.gap: Formal organization policies, final SSP, CUI scope, and external assessment evidence remain separate requirements.

records.title: High availability, backup, restore, and failover evidence
records.implementation: Gate 31 requires candidate-bound cryptographic HA evidence rather than accepting availability claims without retained artifacts.
records.gap: Provider-backed availability, backup/restore, failover, RPO and RTO artifacts are not yet complete; Florida Class D production remains fail closed.

records.title: Regulated Class D separation from generic commerce
records.implementation: Generic Academy checkout, redemption, and Stripe fulfillment do not activate Florida Class D. Regulated mutations execute through a dedicated pre-identity fail-closed boundary and production activation remains separately governed.
records.gap: Class D production still requires licensing, fresh candidate-bound UAT, production database promotion, HA/recovery evidence, rollback evidence, and explicit activation prerequisites.

records.title: GitHub protected-branch enforcement gap
records.implementation: The repository uses governed PR workflows and exact-SHA validation, but direct control-plane inspection continues to report main unprotected, required status-check enforcement off, and no repository ruleset. GitHub issue #60 is the controlled administrator work item.
records.gap: An authorized GitHub administrator must enable and retain evidence of main-branch protection/ruleset enforcement, required checks, no force push/deletion, and governed bypass handling before this control is closed.

records.title: GitHub code security, disclosure, and dependency monitoring
records.implementation: CodeQL Advanced scans GitHub Actions and JavaScript/TypeScript, SECURITY.md defines Obserra coordinated vulnerability reporting, and Dependabot version-update configuration reviews npm and GitHub Actions dependencies weekly.
records.boundary: GitHub repository and code security services
records.gap: Dependabot alerts were reported disabled by the API, and secret-scanning/push-protection state is not verifiable through the current integration. GitHub issue #60 retains these owner-admin actions.

records.title: Vercel production deployment integrity and dependency lock parity
records.implementation: A Vercel-recognized lib sentinel binds proxy.ts changes to production deployment relevance, CI verifies the exact Git blob identity, and package-lock.json is retained in the Vercel build context so production dependency resolution matches the audited lockfile.
records.boundary: GitHub CI and Vercel production deployment
records.gap: The Vercel project Ignored Build Step remains provider-side configuration; the source sentinel prevents the observed proxy-skip failure under the current rule, but future project-setting changes require revalidation.

records.title: Production incident recovery and external identity failure containment
records.implementation: The production HTTP 500 incident was traced across Clerk initialization, Vercel routing/build-skip behavior, and dependency-lock parity. Remediation isolates public availability from identity-provider failure, retains fail-closed protected access, records failed intermediate releases, and binds the recovered runtime to an exact merge SHA and deployment ID.
records.boundary: Obserra application, GitHub CI, Vercel, and Clerk
records.gap: Formal organizational incident-response exercise evidence and provider assurance remain separate assessment evidence.
